policy.comment: @policy: is the one reserved keyword the parser dispatches on directly.

entry-point.comment: @entry-point/@entry-point(label) is recognized by the parser as a structural marker, not free text.

data-entry-header.comment: identifier data (summary): - the 'data' marker and a non-empty parenthesized summary are required grammar; the summary's own text is free prose and stays unstyled.

named-entry-header.comment: identifier (summary): - a non-empty parenthesized summary is required grammar; the summary's own text is free prose and stays unstyled.

generic-header.comment: Folder/File/Class header. Only the name and trailing colon are enforced; any hint text after the name is explicitly not enforced (llmlang-format.md §1) and is left unstyled.

flow-entry-header.comment: A generated .llmflow entry-point header - always unindented, a real structural position, not a word match.

commentary-bullet.comment: # is a real content prefix the parser recognizes.

test-bullet.comment: ~ is a real content prefix the parser recognizes.

arrow-call.comment: → call is a real content prefix the parser recognizes. Everything after it (a canonical name, or an external 'via' description) is free text with no further parser-level structure, so it's left unstyled rather than splitting on the word 'via'.

arrow-return.comment: ← return is a real content prefix the parser recognizes (the dash-leader form is the generator's own rendering of it in .llmflow output). The returned text itself is free-form and left unstyled.

behavior-bullet.comment: - is a real content prefix. Its text is free-form prose - no word within it (accepts/returns/checks whether/if yes/repeats/etc.) is recognized or required by the parser, so none of it is styled differently from any other word.
